title: Blue Gold: an exhibition review
text:
The exhibition 'Blue Gold' at the City Museum {A} the history of denim, from rough work clothes to the symbol of rebellion. It begins in a gold-rush camp, where a tailor and his partner {B} reinforcing trouser pockets with metal rivets. Visitors can examine a pair of trousers from that period, {C} faded and patched beyond recognition. The curators have also borrowed objects from three countries, including a letter in which a miner complains about the price of his trousers, and a recorded commentary helps those who prefer listening to reading.

The second room is the best one. Films and photographs show how young people in the 1950s adopted jeans {D}. Parents were alarmed, schools banned them, and the clothes became a statement of independence.

Not everything works. The final section, {E}, feels hurried and repeats ideas from the first rooms. Still, {F} anybody interested in how clothes shape identity should spend an afternoon here.
